specs.keyboard_notes: Magic Keyboard, Touch ID, Force Touch trackpad

battery.notes: 100Wh; 140W adapter but input capped ~97W. NBC: battery dropped 12% in one hour of full load even with stronger PSUs.

offers.name: Apple MacBook Pro 16.2" (2026) - Space Black (Apple M5 Max / 36GB RAM / 2TB SSD) - English

reviews.quote: the larger 16-inch chassis handles the powerful M5 Max much better compared to the MacBook Pro 14 and the performance is both better as well as more consistent. However, even the MacBook Pro 16 cannot utilize the full potential of the M5 Max and the cooling system can only handle 70 Watts.
outstanding build quality with premium materials and incredible fit and finish

praises: M5 Max performance is far more consistent in the 16-inch than the 14-inch (NBC head-to-head)
36GB unified memory + 32-core GPU handles 4K/8K multitrack timelines and mid-size local LLMs (NBC-class tests)
Cooling unit is usually very quiet or even inaudible (NBC)
Mini-LED panel still keeps up with the best tandem-OLED panels in brightness and color accuracy (NBC)
Thunderbolt 5, PCIe 5.0 SSD, and the best speakers in any laptop (NBC)
complaints: Cooling can only handle 70W — the M5 Max still isn't fully unleashed even here (NBC)
Power delivery limited to ~97W; battery drops 12% in an hour of full load even with bigger PSUs (NBC)
The current chassis and cooling unit need a redesign (NBC)
Wi-Fi 7 module only supports 160 MHz, capping rates at ~2 Gbps (NBC)
C$5,999 with soldered RAM/SSD; considering the prices you pay, these limitations are not ideal (NBC)

design_philosophy: Apple's flagship-size workstation at the entry Max tier: 36GB unified memory and a 32-core GPU for professional media and AI work, in the chassis that (per NBC) hosts the Max chip most gracefully. It buys most of the Max's capability while the Pro tier handles everything below it.
rating_notes: Ratings inferred from NBC's 92.4% review of the 16-inch M5 Max (40-core GPU test unit): −0.3 gaming / −0.3 creative_work / −0.3 ai_ml for the 32-core/36GB tier per NOTES GPU/memory tiering. Thermals capped (7.5) because NBC found the chassis cooling limited to 70W — better than the 14-inch Max (5.5) but not full Max potential.
